correctness.rationale: The incidence criterion follows from a complete three-case classification of pairs of unselected cells and selected-cell total-neighbor counts; both ways are proved. Labelled-component exponential-sieve formulas follow formally. The sharp lower bound is attained by explicit bipartite-tree components and equality forces all optimum components to be trees. Independent direct subset enumeration checks both code predicates and component criteria on small rook graphs; a separate exact-integer coefficient calculation checks cardinality distributions and isolated-edge polynomial recurrence. Finite checks are not substituted for the universal proof.

value.rationale: For all two-factor complete-graph Cartesian products this gives a natural exact all-cardinality classification and enumeration of sensor codes, an isolated-component bijection separating ordinary and total codes, a parity/congruence-like one-sensor aspect-ratio transition, and complete forest-based counts of optimal codes. These go materially beyond previously known scalar ordinary location-domination numbers and two-row special cases; they make exact future comparisons and optimal-placement sampling possible.
